title: States Move to Limit Access to H.I.V. Treatment
partialText: Citing shortfalls in federal support, about 20 states are toughening eligibility requirements for patients in drug assistance programs.

title: Tariffs Force Down Heavy Equipment Sales and Jobs
partialText: An industry report shows high interest rates, fewer infrastructure projects and tariffs pressures have slowed growth and decreased jobs in the sector.

title: Airline Stocks Tumble as Iran War Expands Across Middle East
partialText: Higher fuel prices and lower demand for international flights are eating into airlines’ profits.

title: The Pentagon’s Favorite Tech Guy Is This Hawaiian Shirt-Wearing Founder
partialText: Palmer Luckey, who founded the defense tech start-up Anduril, has become the It Guy as President Trump aims to modernize the U.S. military with autonomous weapons.

title: The Costs of the Attacks on Iran
partialText: Rising oil prices, volatile stocks and potentially higher inflation are all weighing on investors’ minds as the military campaign continues.

title: Beyond a Trade War, China, Japan and Others in Asia Face a New Energy Threat
partialText: China and its neighbors scrambled to soften the blow of a disorderly trade war. Conflict in the Middle East now threatens to disrupt the oil imports that power their economies.

title: Antitrust Trial to Challenge Live Nation’s Grip on the Music Industry
partialText: A jury will decide whether the music colossus, which owns venues, represents artists and operates Ticketmaster, is a monopoly, as the Justice Department contends.

title: A Crisis in the Alps: Airbnb, Climate Change and Americans
partialText: The mountains’ resort towns have reached an inflection point, facing changes that threaten their cultures and even survival, as demand for short-term rentals reshapes the landscape.

title: In Alysa Liu and Eileen Gu, China and America See a Mirror Image
partialText: The Olympic athletes are the subject of uncomfortable public comparisons that present online narratives that overlap more than both sides may realize.

title: Global Stock Markets Fall After U.S.-Israel Attack on Iran
partialText: The strikes come at a precarious time for stocks, forcing investors to weigh the fallout of a potential prolonged disruption to oil supplies and logistics.

title: Oil Prices Surge After Iran Attack
partialText: How long prices remain high will depend on what the United States, Israel and Iran do next.

title: Are ‘Bossware’ Tools Tracking You?
partialText: In recent years, the technologies used to surveil workers have become more sophisticated and widespread.

title: Kickstarter’s C.E.O. on Running a Fully Remote Company With a Four-Day Workweek
partialText: Everette Taylor took over Kickstarter at a low moment for the crowdfunding pioneer, which made its name with small projects but now attracts major multinationals and celebrities.

title: 40 Years and 10,000 Broadcasts In, They’re Still Live on Air
partialText: Rick Ardon and Susannah Carr have been delivering the news together in Western Australia since 1985 — a Guinness World Record.

title: Oil Shipments in Persian Gulf Already Disrupted by Iran Attack
partialText: Tankers have begun to steer clear of the region and the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to push up energy prices.

title: Berkshire Hathaway Posts a Drop in Earnings in Buffett’s Last Year
partialText: In his first report as C.E.O., Gregory Abel, stuck to a straight commentary rather than Warren Buffett’s folksy tone. The lower earnings were largely driven by declines in the insurance business.

title: Banks Are Becoming Bulwarks for Vulnerable Seniors
partialText: Older Americans are losing billions of dollars annually to financial exploitation. Banks and investment firms are training employees to spot red flags and stop the transactions.

title: Lloyd Blankfein on Trump, Epstein and Life After Goldman Sachs
partialText: In a wide-ranging interview with Andrew Ross Sorkin, Goldman’s former C.E.O. discussed his life and new memoir.

title: Netflix Lost Warner. Maybe That’s a Good Thing.
partialText: It is entirely possible, analysts say, that Netflix will be better off by bailing from its $83 billion deal with Warner Bros. Discovery.

title: Warner Bros. Employees Glum About Prospect of Paramount Ownership
partialText: Employees at the company had started to warm to the idea of Netflix as its corporate owner. Now they face the prospect of major cuts under Paramount.

title: QAnon Faithful See Validation in the Epstein Files
partialText: The nearly decade-old conspiracy theory does not align neatly with the facts emerging from the documents. That does not seem to matter.

title: 4 Ways to Enjoy Your Savings in Retirement Without Going Broke
partialText: Once paychecks stop, it can be frightening to shift out of the savings habit. But there are strategies to enjoy your nest egg and make it last.

title: New Geothermal Technology Aims to Produce Clean Energy in Germany
partialText: Developers are using a new geothermal technology in Germany to produce clean energy.

title: In a Memoir Draft, Changpeng Zhao of Binance Details the Talks Leading to His Prison Time
partialText: In a draft of his memoir, Changpeng Zhao, the founder of Binance, laid out the secret negotiations that led to his imprisonment and a run-in with ICE.

title: Justice Dept. Tries to Slow Down Legal Battle Over Tariff Refunds
partialText: Earlier, President Trump suggested on social media that he could try to persuade the Supreme Court to reconsider its rejection of his tariffs.

title: Instagram to Alert Parents to Teens’ Self-Harm Searches
partialText: Parents will receive notifications if a child has used the platform repeatedly to search for terms related to suicide or self-harm, but users must opt in to get them.

title: Iris Cantor, Philanthropist and Art Collector, Dies at 95
partialText: She and her husband, the financier B. Gerald Cantor, amassed one of the largest private collections of Rodin artworks, donating much of it to museums around the world.

title: How David Zaslav Pulled Off the Sale of Warner Bros. Discovery to Paramount
partialText: Not long ago, Mr. Zaslav was widely criticized for his management of Warner Bros. Discovery. He overcame the doubters, cementing a blockbuster sale to Paramount.

title: Overlooked No More: Bobby Garnett, ‘Godfather’ of Vintage Dealers
partialText: His store, Bobby From Boston, transformed the way vintage men’s wear is sold, serving as a model for a generation of retailers.

title: Pentagon-Anthropic Standoff Is a Decisive Moment for How A.I. Will Be Used in War
partialText: The Pentagon’s contract dispute with Anthropic is part of a wider clash about the use of artificial intelligence for national security and who decides on any safeguards.

title: Trump Media Explores Spinning Off Truth Social
partialText: The move would split off the money-losing social media platform as the company pursues a merger with a fusion power company.

title: OpenAI Raises $110 Billion Led by Amazon, Nvidia and SoftBank, Extending A.I. Boom
partialText: Amazon, Nvidia and SoftBank led the investment, valuing the parent of ChatGPT at $730 billion.

title: The I.R.S. Shut Its Direct File, but Here Are Other Free Filing Options
partialText: The agency still offers a Free File program that works with commercial tax software firms. Some companies also offer free tools for certain filers.

title: E.U. Pushes Ahead With South American Trade Deal Despite Legal Challenge
partialText: The provisional application of the agreement with Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay is intended to diversify Europe’s trading relationships.

title: Paramount Is Set to Win Warner Bros. Now Comes the Hard Part.
partialText: The media company controlled by the Ellisons out-dueled Netflix for control of Warner Bros. Discovery. The next step is making the combined media empires work.

title: How India Became One of the World’s Biggest Economies
partialText: India has grown rapidly despite its slow industrialization, and its economy is now nearly as big as Japan’s.

title: For CNN, a Takeover by Paramount Means a Suddenly Uncertain Future
partialText: Paramount’s apparent victory over Netflix in securing Warner Bros. Discovery has led to concerns within the CNN newsroom about editorial independence.

title: What Larry and David Ellison Would Own After Warner Bros. Takeover
partialText: If Paramount can close its deal to buy Warner Bros. Discovery, Larry and David Ellison will influence nearly every corner of news, entertainment and tech.

title: A World Where All Is Free? That’s Elon Musk’s Theory of ‘Sustainable Abundance.’
partialText: The Tesla and SpaceX chief has told his followers that they will live in a world where robots will take care of every need and people do not have to work, in what has become his latest slogan.

title: The Web of Companies Owned by Elon Musk
partialText: In mapping out Elon Musk’s wealth, our investigation found that Mr. Musk is behind more than 90 companies in Texas. Kirsten Grind, a New York Times Investigations reporter, explains what her team found.

title: The Rise and Fall of a 3-D Printing Empire
partialText: Desktop Metal, a billion-dollar start-up, promised to revolutionize manufacturing. It went bankrupt, and now has much humbler ambitions as the 3-D printing industry takes a sober turn.

title: Elon Musk’s Secret Web of Companies in Texas
partialText: The megabillionaire was tied to about 90 companies in the state, which he uses for everything from paying nannies to buying land to supporting Donald Trump’s re-election, according to a Times examination.

title: Honolulu on a Budget
partialText: Hawaii is expensive, but basing yourself in the capital, where local culture and nature are within easy reach, can save you money on lodgings and food, leaving funds for a few splurges.

title: South Korea Clears Way for Google Maps to Fully Operate
partialText: South Korea approved Google’s request to export detailed map data, reversing a longstanding restriction that made the tool largely nonfunctional.

title: With a New Nigeria Refinery, Africa’s Richest Man Wants ‘to Rescue the Country’
partialText: Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest man, has an ambitious vision for the continent’s most populous nation, but hurdles stand in his way.

title: India Built the World’s Back Office. A.I. Is Starting to Shrink It.
partialText: Artificial intelligence promises to automate the white-collar work that made India a tech powerhouse. The country is racing to adapt before it’s too late.

title: Germany’s Oil and Gas Output Is Dwindling as Prices Rise
partialText: Natural gas production in Germany has fallen about 80 percent in the past two decades even as the country seeks to replace flows from Russia.

title: 32.6 Million Watched Trump’s State of the Union Address, Nielsen Says
partialText: The audience was roughly on par with former President Biden’s final State of the Union address in 2024.

title: Block Cuts 40% of Its Work Force Because of Its Embrace of A.I.
partialText: About 4,000 workers will lose their jobs as the payments company does more work with new artificial intelligence tools, its top executive said.
